episodes.188784: A warm front draped along central West Virginia and central Virginia provided the focus for a few thunderstorms to develop during the late afternoon.  One of these storms became severe and produced large hail in Rockbridge County.
episodes.188785: A deepening low with an associated mature cyclone came to California on March 29, with widespread rain associated with the system. Continuing instability the next day resulted in noticeable thunderstorms with hail reported in several places across the Bay Area, including Walnut Creek, Belmont, and south of San Jose. In Monterey County, significant rainfall contributed to a landslide that forced the closure of California Highway 1 north of Big Sur.
episodes.188802: Gusty daytime west-southwesterly winds ahead of a cold frontal passage boosted temperatures nearly 20 degrees above normal, with an afternoon high of 79 at the Lawrenceville-Vincennes Airport.  Scattered evening thunderstorms developed along the slowly-passing front along the Ohio Valley, with severe weather within central Indiana confined to large hail from one cell in Knox County.
episodes.189098: An isolated supercell thunderstorm produced marginally severe hail over portions of the central Virginia Piedmont.
episodes.189099: Remnant outflow from decaying convection resulting in dry microbursts of gale- to storm-force during the late evening hours.
episodes.189194: A supercell thunderstorm developed along a warm front just south of Macomb during the early evening of March 31st.  The storm tracked southeastward, continuously dropping 1 to 2-inch diameter hail from southern Fulton County to western Douglas County before gradually weakening well after dark.  The largest hail stones measuring 2.5 inches in diameter fell on the northeast side of Decatur in Macon County.
episodes.189599: A combination of snow melt and heavy rain led to minor flooding along the Mattawamkeag River. Flooding developed during the early morning hours of the 31st. The river crested less than a half foot above flood stage during the afternoon of the 31st. The river then remained at around crest levels with minor flooding persisting into early April. The flooding mostly impacted low land areas along the river.
episodes.189634: A stationary boundary set up across portions of Southern Illinois and Southwest Indiana near I-64 and became a focal point for shower and thunderstorm development for the evening hours on the 30th with a few storms producing sub-severe hail. RAP analysis had 0-1 km CAPE of 500-750 J/kg and 0-6 km shear of 50 kts to go with lapse rates around 8 C/km.
episodes.189635: A stationary boundary set up across portions of Southern Illinois and Southwest Indiana near I-64 and became a focal point for shower and thunderstorm development for the evening hours on the 30th with a few storms producing hail. RAP analysis had 0-1 km CAPE of 500-750 J/kg and 0-6 km shear of 50 kts to go with lapse rates around 8 C/km.
episodes.189651: Widespread showers and storms were seen through March 31, with one severe storm that tracked through southeast Iowa, northeast Missouri, and through central Illinois. This storm was a long lived supercell thunderstorm that produced hail upwards to ping pong ball sized in Macomb Illinois, with tennis ball sized as this storm progressed through central Illinois.
episodes.189652: Widespread showers and storms were seen through March 31, with one severe storm that tracked through southeast Iowa, northeast Missouri, and through central Illinois. This storm was a long lived supercell thunderstorm that produced hail upwards to ping pong ball sized in Macomb Illinois, with tennis ball sized as this storm progressed through central Illinois.
episodes.189653: Widespread showers and storms were seen through March 31, with one severe storm that tracked through southeast Iowa, northeast Missouri, and through central Illinois. This storm was a long lived supercell thunderstorm that produced hail upwards to ping pong ball sized in Macomb Illinois, with tennis ball sized as this storm progressed through central Illinois.
episodes.189821: A stationary frontal boundary parked over West Virginia contributed to strong thunderstorms on the evening of March 30th. An upper level disturbance traveling along the boundary helped to spark convection around southeast Ohio that afternoon, which then migrated into parts of northeast West Virginia. A few storms grew to severe levels, and yielded instances of damaging wind gusts that led to downed trees as well as hail between half an inch to an inch in diameter. Activity was diurnally driven, and weakened tremendously after sunset.
episodes.189823: A few strong thunderstorms sprouted in southeast Ohio on the afternoon of March 30th in response to a stalled frontal boundary draped through the area. An upper level disturbance provided enough energy to work alongside daytime heating in order to create scattered convection around the Ohio River Valley. Storms grew tall enough to produce dime to nickel size hail across portions of Perry and Washington County. These storms would go on to become severe as they traveled eastward through West Virginia that afternoon and evening.
episodes.189855: A strong low pressure system and an associated atmospheric river impacted Southern California on March 30th and 31st. This event saw impacts in the forms of heavy rain, some scattered thunderstorms, and snow to mountain communities above 5000 feet in elevation.
episodes.189883: A trough of low pressure over the region and cold air aloft fueled scattered thunderstorms over the Mojave Desert. One storm produced a large amount of graupel.
episodes.190520: Ahead of a front dropping south through Indiana, a broken line of convection worked its way through southern Indiana. This resulted in one tree being reported down in Dubois County.
episodes.195298: The most powerful storm of March brought significant rain, mountain snow, strong thunderstorms and flash flooding to Southwestern California. Rainfall totals ranged from 1.50 to 4.00 inches across coastal and valley areas and up to 7 inches across the mountain slopes. At higher elevations, over 1 foot of snowfall was reported across the Ventura and Los Angeles county mountains. Strong thunderstorms generated gusty outflow winds and heavy rain which caused numerous reports of flash flooding.
